title: Quantum chaos and late-time equipartition of symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity
authors: Jayashish Das, Suman Das, Juan F. Pedraza, Le-Chen Qu
abstract: We study symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity in finite-dimensional chaotic quantum many-body systems. When both the Hamiltonian and the initial operator commute with a conserved charge, the operator dynamics decomposes into independent symmetry sectors, each with its own Krylov chain. We show that, after saturation, the unresolved Krylov complexity is additive over symmetry sectors. In the absence of additional Liouvillian degeneracies, the late-time contribution of a sector with Hilbert-space dimension $d_q$ is controlled by $d_q(d_q-1)$, leading to a dimension-weighted equipartition that approaches the simple large-sector scaling $d_q^2/\sum_{q'}d_{q'}^2$. This late-time rule differs from the early-time weighted-average discussed in the literature and is governed instead by the dimensions of the accessible operator spaces. We support the analytic prediction with numerical studies of the real and complex SYK models, a chaotic bosonic spin model, and the mixed-field Ising chain. Our results show that resolving exact symmetries is essential for interpreting the saturation value of Krylov complexity as a diagnostic of chaotic operator growth.
summary: This paper analyzes how quantum chaos manifests in many-body systems by studying symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity. It proves that in the late-time limit, the total complexity is simply the sum of the complexities from each independent symmetry sector. This finding offers a robust, dimension-dependent diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum chaos beyond simple early-time growth measurements.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum chaos and the late-time equipartition of symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity in finite-dimensional quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The late-time Krylov complexity is found to be additive over independent symmetry sectors, leading to a dimension-weighted equipartition scaling distinct from early-time predictions.
method: The analysis employs the Krylov complexity, which measures operator growth via the Liouvillian superoperator, and decomposes the dynamics by exploiting conserved symmetries.
model_or_system: The work applies to general chaotic quantum many-body systems, with numerical verification using the real and complex SYK models, a chaotic bosonic spin model, and the mixed-field Ising chain.
key_observables: Krylov complexity ($C_K$), symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity ($C_q^K$), and the late-time saturation value of these complexities.
important_parameters: The late-time saturation regime ($t_{	ext{sat}} \lesssim t \ll t_{	ext{rec}}$) and the dimensions of the accessible operator spaces ($d_q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the absence of additional Liouvillian degeneracies and relies on the late-time delocalization of the Krylov wavefunction.
figures_summary: Figure 6 compares the standard Arnoldi vs. modified Lanczos construction for the mixed-field Ising chain, demonstrating the modified algorithm correctly identifies the true full Krylov dimension.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general framework by defining symmetry-resolved Krylov complexity, proves the additivity of the complexity in the late-time limit, and supports these analytic predictions with numerical studies on several specific quantum spin models.
why_interesting: The focus on complexity measures and their late-time saturation provides a powerful, quantifiable diagnostic tool for characterizing the transition between integrable and chaotic regimes in complex quantum systems.
